## What changes, and why

<!--
The defect or the need, then the change. If it fixes an issue, `Closes #N`.

The "why" is the part that survives: in a year the diff will be readable and
the reason will not be, unless it is written down.
-->

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature (a new engine, a step, a knob, a format)
- [ ] Threshold or default changed — **the measurement section below is mandatory**
- [ ] Refactor with no behaviour change
- [ ] Documentation, notebooks or examples
- [ ] CI, packaging or governance

## Which interface or extension point does it touch

- [ ] The engine contract (`engines/base.py`: `transcribe_page`, `read_page`, `available`, `register`)
- [ ] The step contract (`steps/base.py`: `name`, `run(ctx) -> StepResult`, `expensive`)
- [ ] The acceptance gate (`quality/gate.py`) — the *single* criterion, shared by the step and the cascade
- [ ] The replacement gate (`quality/rejection.py`) — runs only after an expensive step
- [ ] The vetoes (`quality/vetoes.py`) — what runs *before* paying for an expensive step
- [ ] The cascade's ordering or the contest between candidates (`cascade.py`)
- [ ] `Config` — a field added, removed or re-typed
- [ ] The public API re-exported from `autosxtract/__init__.py`
- [ ] The CLI (`autosxtract extract | diagnose | download-models`)
- [ ] The pattern catalogue (`autosxtract/patterns/` and its TOML packs) or the lexicon — the adaptation seam
- [ ] Packaging: dependencies, extras, platform markers
- [ ] None of the above

<!--
The layering is a hard rule, not a style: pdf/ knows only the file, quality/
does no I/O, engines/ does not know what a cascade is, steps/ composes the two.
An import crossing an arrow backwards is a design break — say so here if the
change needed one, and expect the review to look for another shape.
-->

## The measurement behind any changed number

<!--
DELETE THIS SECTION ONLY IF THE DIFF CHANGES NO NUMBER.

Every threshold in `config.py` carries the measurement that fixed it. A number
changed without one cannot be reviewed — nobody, including its author six
months later, can tell whether it was calibrated or guessed. This is the
project's hardest rule and the one it most wants to make expensive to break.

State, for each number:

  * the old value and the new one;
  * the corpus: how many documents, of what kind, from where (no identifiers);
  * what got better and what got worse, in numbers;
  * how it was measured, with the command.

And the methodological trap, which has already caught this project once: AN
ISOLATED MEASUREMENT LIES. Turning Vision's language correction off improved
anchors on 60 documents (+4) and destroyed them across the whole cascade
(-227), because the worse text failed the gate and fell to worse engines. What
decides is the CASCADE's behaviour, not one engine's output.
`scripts/compare_engines.py` measures both — report both.
-->

- [ ] This pull request changes no threshold, default or magic number.
- [ ] It does, and the measurement is written above, in the code comment beside the number, and covers the cascade — not just the engine in isolation.

| number | old | new | corpus | effect on the engine | effect on the cascade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

## Tests

- [ ] New tests cover the change, and they fail without it.
- [ ] A bug fix carries a regression test that reproduces the original defect.
- [ ] Any new fixture is **synthetic**, generated by PyMuPDF with invented text (`tests/conftest.py`). No real document, ever.
- [ ] Tests needing a real engine or a slow path are marked (`slow`, `apple`, `paddle`) so the bare-core suite stays green.

<!--
The suite has to pass on a bare `pip install autosxtract[dev]`, because that is
how most people will have it. A test that silently requires an engine turns
somebody else's CI red for a reason they cannot act on.
-->

## Checks

- [ ] `make all` is green locally (`lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `privacy`).
- [ ] `make lint` specifically — **both** halves: `ruff check` does not verify formatting, and running only it leaves CI red with the tree green.
- [ ] `pre-commit` is installed (`make hooks`) and ran on this branch.

<!--
Careful with pre-commit: it stashes unstaged changes and inspects WHAT WILL BE
COMMITTED, not your working tree. Fixing a file without `git add` leaves the
hook looking at the old version.
-->

## Privacy

- [ ] `make privacy` passes, and I understand it is the only check here that prevents a leak rather than merely a red build.
- [ ] No PDF, CSV, JSONL, spreadsheet, model weight or extracted text is added by this diff.
- [ ] No real case number, tax ID, company ID, name, address, institutional path or internal host appears anywhere — **including in comments, docstrings and commit messages**.
- [ ] Any identifier used as an example has an **invalid check digit** on purpose, so the scanner stays quiet and nobody has to judge case by case whether a real one exists.

## Networking

- [ ] This diff adds no networking to the default cascade.
- [ ] It adds no host, port, URL or credential field to `Config`.
- [ ] If it touches a remote step, the `url` remains a **constructor argument** with no default, no environment-variable discovery and no fallback endpoint.

<!--
The previous version of this pipeline reached its OCR engine over a reverse SSH
tunnel. The worker went down and the text SILENTLY degraded: 488 documents
re-extracted down the worse path, 19.5 minutes instead of 4.9, 28,239
characters lost, and nobody noticed until somebody checked. A remote step
nobody declared must not exist.
-->

## Public API and compatibility

- [ ] Nothing exported from `autosxtract/__init__.py` changed name, signature or semantics.
- [ ] Or it did, and this is a breaking change: describe the migration below and confirm the version bump is MAJOR (or that we are pre-1.0 and it goes in the changelog as breaking).
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry under `## [Unreleased]`.

## Documentation

- [ ] README, `docs/` and any affected notebook are updated in this same pull request.
- [ ] A new default, engine, step or extension point is documented **where the reader will look for it**, and the documentation says why, not only how.
- [ ] `tests/test_documentation.py` still passes — it reads the README and checks every public name it promises actually exists.
- [ ] A decision that will be non-obvious in six months is recorded in `CLAUDE.md`, with the consequence that fixed it.

## Review

Two code owners are requested automatically (`.github/CODEOWNERS`). A change to
a gate, to the engine contract, to `config.py`, to the privacy scanner or to a
workflow gets read line by line — those are the files where a mistake is
silent rather than loud.
